stories.title: Italian Kitchen Manufacturer Officine Gullo to Open Store at 95 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Hey now, hey now, these kitchens are what dreams are made of. Italy’s Officine Gullo, a manufacturer of luxury commercial and residential kitchens, has taken 3,200 square feet of ground-floor retail space at Sunlight Development’s 95 Madison Avenue in Manhattan’s NoMad neighborhood, Commercial Observer has learned. The 10-year lease represents Officine Gullo’s new flagship space in New York City. The asking rent was not disclosed, but the average asking rent for retail space around nearby Herald Square was $403 per square foot during the third quarter of 2026, according to CBRE data. Ross Kaplan and William Chaplin from Newmark represented the tenant on this lease, according to a source close to the deal, while Harvest International‘s Daphne Zhou-Chan represented the landlord. Newmark declined Commercial Observer’s request for comment, while Zhou-Chan did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It is unclear when the Florence-based Officine Gullo will open at its new 95 Madison Avenue location, which will be its second in New York City following its showroom at 157 Hudson Street in Tribeca. The firm did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. Built in 1912, 95 Madison Avenue is a luxury condo development at the corner of Madison Avenue and East 29th Street. The exterior of the property was designed by FXCollaborative, while the interior was designed by Paris Forino. Amenities at the residence include a lounge with a marble fireplace, a children’s playroom, a professional-quality music room to jam in, as well as fitness and wellness spaces. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Officine Gullo (Italian kitchen mfg.) leases 3,200 SF at 95 Madison, NoMad Manhattan.
Herald Square retail asking rent: $403/SF in Q3 2026; strong luxury retail demand.
10-year lease signals sustained high-end residential amenity demand in Manhattan.
stories.summary: Italy's luxury kitchen manufacturer Officine Gullo has signed a 10-year ground-floor lease at Sunlight Development's 95 Madison Avenue in NoMad, taking 3,200 SF as its flagship NYC location. Asking rent around Herald Square averaged $403/SF in Q3 2026, reflecting elevated retail pricing. The deal underscores continued demand for premium residential amenity tenants in central Manhattan submarkets.
stories.impact: NoMad and surrounding Midtown South submarkets remain desirable for high-end residential users; strong luxury retail leasing signals renters in new or Class A multifamily are willing to pay for curated lifestyle services nearby. Developers should note sustained retail depth in these zones supports higher multifamily rents and unit mix premiums.

stories.title: David Werner Buys 49% Stake in 605 Third Avenue

Werner, an avid buyer and redeveloper of office properties in Midtown, has acquired a 49 percent stake in 605 Third Avenue, a 43-story, 1 million-square-foot office tower he now owns in tandem with Fisher Brothers, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. It’s unclear how much Werner paid to acquire the stake, but J.P. Morgan Asset Management — Fisher Brothers’ previous partner at the property — listed the 49 percent stake at a valuation of $425 million in July. Newmark’s Adam Spies, Joshua King, Adam Doneger, Doug Harmon, Marcella Fasulo and Avery Silverstein brokered the deal. Fisher Brothers declined to comment, while a spokesperson for Newmark did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Werner could not be reached for comment. The Real Deal first reported the deal. While Werner is a household name in Manhattan’s office-to-residential conversion scene — such as at the former Pfizer headquarters building at 219-235 East 42nd Street — he will not be pursuing any conversion plans at 605 Third Avenue and plans to keep it as an office property, the source said. Current office tenants at 605 Third Avenue include law firms Hodgson Russ and Katsky Korins, as well as business publishing and events company Informa. The deal marks Werner’s second traditional office play in Midtown over the past year, after buying One Dag Hammarskjöld Plaza from Rockpoint for $270 million last December. Werner’s stake acquisition in 605 Third Avenue also comes as Fisher Brothers withdrew its Israeli bond market offering after failing to raise interest from investors overseas and citing challenges from rising interest rates and changes in market conditions, TRD reported. bullets: David Werner acquires 49% stake in 605 Third Avenue, 1M SF Midtown office tower.
J.P. Morgan Asset Management's 49% stake valued at $425M (July 2026).

JPMorgan's previous 49% stake was valued at $425M in July 2026. The deal suggests Werner sees conversion or value-add opportunity in core Midtown office stock.
stories.impact: Werner's move signals continued executive conviction in Midtown office-to-residential conversion arbitrage, even in a high-rate environment. Developers should monitor if Werner pursues conversion or mixed-use redevelopment; success would validate Midtown Central's repositioning potential and could unlock capital and entitlements for similar large-block office-to-multifamily plays in Manhattan core.

stories.title: SL Green Reports High Q3 Earnings From Sales of Two Manhattan Properties
stories.excerpt: SL Green Realty recorded strong balance sheet performance during the third quarter of 2026 despite high interest rates and slower quarter-over-quarter leasing. This was mainly from the company’s disposition strategy, which generated additional cash flow. SL Green completed the August sale of 10 East 53rd Street to Jeffrey Kaplan’s Meadow Partners for $312.2 million, from which it collected net proceeds of $99 million. In September, it offloaded 110 Greene Street to Natora Group for $226 million, for which it will see $216 million in proceeds. The real estate investment trust said Thursday that funds from operations reached $122.1 million during the third quarter, compared to $109.6 million in the second quarter and $120.4 million in the third quarter of 2025. Meanwhile, total revenue was $273 million, an increase from $241 million recorded in the second quarter and $244 million reported in the third quarter of 2025. Net income was $72.2 million as compared to $26.5 million in the second quarter and $24.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, SL Green said during an earnings call. “Higher rates impact all real estate businesses and most every industry, and we’re talking about a swing of about 150 basis points throughout the year, up from the already elevated levels at the beginning of the year,” SL Green CEO Marc Holliday said during the earnings call. “That, of course, is not something we control, and we’ve noted in the earnings release that it had a 25-cent impact on the back half of the year. However, we can and have aggressively and smartly hedged parts of our liabilities to lock in lower interest rates, so the impact has not been nearly as great as it could have been.” The number of leasing transactions, meanwhile, declined for SL Green in the third quarter, with 38 Manhattan office leases totaling 591,108 square feet. bullets: SL Green sold 10 East 53rd ($312M) and 110 Greene ($226M) in Q3 2026.
Q3 FOO $122.1M (up from $109.6M Q2); net income $72.2M vs. $26.5M Q2.
Office disposition strategy generating liquidity; net proceeds $99M and $216M respectively.
stories.summary: SL Green Realty posted strong Q3 2026 results driven by two major office sales: 10 East 53rd Street to Meadow Partners for $312.2M (netting $99M) and 110 Greene Street to Natora Group for $226M (netting $216M). FOO reached $122.1M, up from Q2's $109.6M, and net income jumped to $72.2M from $26.5M. The REIT's disposition strategy is improving cash flow despite elevated rates and slower leasing.
stories.impact: SL Green's aggressive office exit and cash-generative position in a difficult rate environment suggests Manhattan office values are finding buyers at reduced levels. For multifamily developers, this signals liquidity in the market and potential land/development sites as office holders divest; monitor whether SL Green redeploys proceeds into multifamily or if further office sales pressure valuations and free up sites for residential redevelopment in Manhattan submarkets.

stories.title: Newmark Launches Bridge Lending Program, Finances $35M Loan for Georgia Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Newmark is now getting into the private credit game. The brokerage announced this week that it has launched a new debt and structured finance program that will provide bridge loans to multifamily assets and aims to eventually allow the firm to become an agency lender via Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. Newmark made their first loan out of the program, a $35 million bridge loan to MFP Capital to refinance Independence Place, a 264-unit multifamily asset in Hinesville, Ga. Newmark’s Henry Stimler, Bill Weber and Ricky Warner originated the debt. Sharon Karaffa, president of multifamily debt & structured finance at Newmark, said that a new program focused on short-term bridge debt will draw the brokerage closer to securitized agency lending and provide Newmark clients with “greater flexibility and continuity.” “The introduction of our Multifamily Bridge Program represents an important expansion of our debt and structured finance solutions, strengthening our ability to support clients throughout the financing lifecycle,” said Karaffa. Located at 1300 Independence Place Drive in Hinesville — a Georgia county seat roughly 40 miles southwest of Savannah — Independence Place will feature one-bedroom to four-bedroom units and include a swimming pool and fitness center on site. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Newmark launches bridge lending program; closes $35M loan to MFP Capital (Georgia).
Loan finances Independence Place, 264-unit multifamily in Hinesville, Georgia.
Program aims to lead to Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac agency lending; expands debt continuity.
stories.summary: Newmark has launched a new bridge lending program for multifamily assets and immediately closed a $35M bridge loan to MFP Capital to refinance Independence Place, a 264-unit community in Hinesville, Georgia. The program aims to eventually position Newmark as an agency lender via Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. The initiative provides short-term bridge flexibility and continuity across the financing lifecycle.
stories.impact: Newmark's foray into bridge lending signals tightening agency debt capacity and developer need for non-bank execution speed; this creates opportunity for developers with near-term refinancing or bridge needs, particularly outside Tier-1 metros where agency lending is slower. For developers, the program may lower execution risk and broaden refinancing options, but also suggests underlying agency market stress and potential cap-rate volatility in smaller metros like Hinesville.

stories.title: IT Firm Mphasis Expands by 14K SF at Rudin’s 41 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: Blackstone-backed information technology firm Mphasis has more than doubled its office footprint at 41 Madison Avenue to 27,709 square feet, and tacked on another decade to its tenure. The deal adds 14,151 square feet to Mphasis’ footprint at Rudin’s office tower northeast of Madison Square Park, according to the landlord. Mphasis, headquartered in Bengaluru, India, will expand its New York City office onto the building’s entire 36th floor, while continuing to occupy the 35th floor below. A 10-year extension accompanied the lease deal, first reported by CoStar. The asking rent was not disclosed, but Class A office rents in Midtown South averaged $98.01 per square foot in the third quarter of 2026, according to Colliers. Rudin’s Robert Steinman and Craig Panzirer represented the landlord in-house, while CBRE’s William Iacovelli and Patrick Moroney negotiated on behalf of Mphasis. “Mphasis’ preference was to remain at 41 Madison Avenue,” Iacovelli told Commercial Observer. “And when the opportunity arose to lease the 36th floor alongside its existing 35th-floor space, it was the ideal solution to support the company’s continued growth.” Mphasis arrived at the 42-story Flatiron District tower in April 2021, CO previously reported. The company relocated from 460 Park Avenue South through a 13,558-square-foot sublease with Mission Capital Advisors. Asking rent at the time was in the mid-$70s per square foot. The 560,000-square-foot building sits along Madison Avenue between East 25th and East 26th streets. Other recent moves there include new full-floor leases by digital financial services firm Zip and investment bank BrightTower, as well as a 13,357-square-foot expansion by investment services firm Polar Asset Management Partners. The organization took a disciplined, long-term approach, and that patience ultimately enabled it to secure a more efficient, cohesive and unified workplace within the building. bullets: Mphasis (IT firm, Blackstone-backed) expands 14,151 SF to 27,709 SF total at 41 Madison.
10-year lease extension; occupies entire 36th floor plus existing 35th floor, Midtown South.
Class A Midtown South rents averaged $98.01/SF in Q3 2026.
stories.summary: Blackstone-backed IT firm Mphasis more than doubled its office footprint at Rudin's 41 Madison Avenue, adding 14,151 SF to reach 27,709 SF, and locked a 10-year extension. The company now occupies the entire 36th floor plus its existing 35th-floor space in Midtown South. Class A office rents in the submarket averaged $98.01/SF in Q3 2026.
stories.impact: Mphasis's expansion and long-term commitment signal sustained tech employer demand in Midtown South, validating the submarket's appeal to high-value IT tenants despite broader office headwinds. For multifamily developers, tech tenant clustering in Midtown South drives younger, higher-income renter in-migration; consider acquisition/development sites within 0.3 miles of 41 Madison and surrounding Class A office to capture tech worker rental demand and support higher rents and unit premiums.

stories.title: Florida People & Companies, October 23, 2026
stories.excerpt: Arcadia Real Estate Developers launched sales and leasing at Vitalis Tower, a seven-story medical and professional office development in Aventura. The tower is located at 21291 NE 28th Avenue on a 1.63-acre site, less than 100 yards from Aventura Hospital. Vitalis Tower will feature approximately 114,000 square feet of usable medical and professional office space, with suites starting at approximately 200 square feet and prices starting at $200,000, with the ability to combine units for spaces of up to 30,000 square feet. PGIM’s real estate investment group has provided over $100 million in fixed-rate financing to Continental Realty Corporation for the financing of two multifamily properties located in Tampa, Florida and Nashville, Tennessee. Details of the Tampa property include: Grand Reserve at Tampa Palms, a 390-unit garden-style multifamily property. Amenities include a pool, an outdoor kitchen, a fitness center and a dog-washing station. Grand Reserve additionally features a jacuzzi, tennis court and basketball court. stories.title: Texas People & Companies, October 23, 2026
stories.excerpt: Dallas-based Holt Lunsford Commercial Investments hired Brad Davey as Managing Principal. In this role, Davey will lead acquisitions, with a focus on shallow-bay industrial opportunities. Davey brings more than 20 years of experience acquiring and managing industrial, multifamily, retail, and office assets across the United States. He joins HLCI from Clarion Partners, where he served as Managing Director and senior acquisitions officer for the firm’s Central Region and led more than $2.5 billion in acquisitions. NAI Legacy expanded its footprint into Texas with the $18 million acquisition of a 59,000-square-foot new-construction Tom Thumb grocery store at 3400 N. Belt Line Road in Sunnyvale, approximately 15 miles east of downtown Dallas.  The store opened in December 2025 as Sunnyvale’s first major grocery store, anchoring the town’s Gateway Park retail development.  Welcome Group announced the start of construction of Lower Kirby Business Park, a 25-acre, master-planned industrial campus in Pearland, Texas, and an 87,450-square-foot lease with Thorpe Plant Maintenance & Engineering, the development’s first tenant. Located at 15020 Kirby Drive near the southwest corner of Beltway 8 and State Highway 288, Lower Kirby Business Park will deliver 250,450 square feet of Class A industrial space across four buildings. stories.title: HCA HealthOne to Create Wheat Ridge Health Park
stories.excerpt: HCA HealthONE bought the Wilmore Center at 7615 W. 38th Ave. for $14.5 million. A Cushman & Wakefield team of Jon Hendrickson and Aaron Johnson represented the seller, CentrePoint Properties, in the transaction. The Denver Business Journal reports that CentrePoint purchased the property for $10.25 million in 2021. HCA HealthONE is planning to bring a medical park, including medical office space and emergency services, to Wheat Ridge. The new health park will be adjacent to the provider’s existing Clear Creek Surgery Center at 7809 W. 38th Ave. It aims to expand access to healthcare for patients and families in the area. The two single-story multi-tenant buildings that make up the Wilmore Center span nearly 52,750 square feet on 5.18 acres and include 236 parking spaces. At the time of the sale, Wilmore Center was 84% occupied. The 15 tenants offer a mix of retail, food and medical services, with 68% of the leased area being occupied by medical-related tenants. HCA HealthONE has not yet disclosed its redevelopment plans. . The post HCA HealthOne to Create Wheat Ridge Health Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: HCA HealthOne acquired Wilmore Center (52,750 SF, 5.18 acres) in Wheat Ridge, CO for $14.5M.
CentrePoint Properties purchased property for $10.25M in 2021; 84% occupied at sale.
HCA plans medical office/emergency services expansion adjacent to existing Clear Creek Surgery Center.
stories.summary: HCA HealthOne has purchased the Wilmore Center in Wheat Ridge, Colorado, a 52,750-SF multi-tenant property on 5.18 acres, for $14.5M (CentrePoint paid $10.25M in 2021). The property was 84% occupied with 68% medical-related tenancy. HCA plans to redevelop it into a medical park with medical office and emergency services, adjacent to its existing Clear Creek Surgery Center.
stories.impact: HCA's healthcare consolidation in Wheat Ridge signals sustained employer/anchor demand in the Denver metro west corridor; the redevelopment will drive local job growth and population stability. For multifamily developers, healthcare-anchored employment centers warrant priority acquisition/development sites within 1–2 miles; medical staff and patients generate stable, educated renter demand with above-average household incomes and lower churn—ideal for Class A product in suburban Denver.

stories.title: Cawley CRE Brokers Sale of Carol Stream Industrial Property
stories.excerpt: Cawley Commercial Real Estate (Cawley CRE) facilitated the direct sale of a 29,600-square-foot industrial property at 170 S. Gary Avenue in Carol Stream, Illinois. Mark Wilson represented both the seller and the buyer, High Street Logistics Properties, in the transaction. Situated on 1.90 acres, the Class B industrial property offers a facility with a combination of warehouse, office, and specialized service space. Built in 2005 with quality precast concrete construction, the building features 24-foot clear ceiling heights, six interior loading docks equipped with lifts, and five interior drive-in doors serving three separate bays. A full office renovation completed in 2023 further enhanced the building’s functionality and appeal. Located minutes from Interstate 355, the property offers convenient regional access for contractors and industrial users. “We had a good understanding of the type of investor who would see the value in this property, and High Street Realty stood out as a strong fit,” said Wilson who led the transaction with support from Daniel Cawley, SIOR and Jordan Kwiecinski. The post Cawley CRE Brokers Sale of Carol Stream Industrial Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: High Street Logistics Properties acquired 29,600-SF industrial property in Carol Stream, Illinois.
Class B property on 1.90 acres; built 2005, 24-foot ceiling, six loading docks.

stories.summary: Cawley CRE facilitated the direct sale of a 29,600-SF Class B industrial property at 170 S. Gary Avenue in Carol Stream, Illinois, to High Street Logistics Properties. The property sits on 1.90 acres with 24-foot ceiling heights, six interior loading docks with lifts, and recent 2023 office renovation. It is located minutes from Interstate 355, offering strong regional logistics access.
stories.impact: Continued investor appetite for suburban Chicago light industrial reflects regional supply-chain resilience and e-commerce logistics demand. While industrial-focused, this sale signals active capital deployment in Chicago exurban markets; multifamily developers should consider co-location or mixed-use opportunities near logistics nodes (I-355 corridor), where worker housing demand is rising and underserved.

stories.title: Colliers Represents Bruno’s Self-Storage in Sale of WI Facilities to Inland Real Estate
stories.excerpt: Colliers’ Dan Lynch recently represented Bruno’s Self Storage, LLC in the sale of two Extra Space-managed self-storage facilities in Wisconsin to Inland Real Estate. Together, the properties total 175,825 sqaure feet with 1486 units.The transactions include a 93,650-square-foot facility completed in 2020 with 749 climate-controlled units located at 9001 Wilmot Rd. in Pleasant Prairie, Wisconsin, as well as an 82,175-square-foot property completed in 2019 with 727 climate-controlled units located at 1585 Corporate Center Dr. in West Bend, Wisconsin. The Class A institutional quality facilities are situated in the rapidly growing southern Wisconsin submarket and the Milwaukee metropolitan statistical area, respectively. “Storage remains an attractive asset class for investors, and these transactions further demonstrate that demand for high-quality, well-located self-storage remains robust,” said Lynch. The post Colliers Represents Bruno’s Self-Storage in Sale of WI Facilities to Inland Real Estate appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Inland Real Estate acquired two self-storage facilities from Bruno's Self Storage in Wisconsin.
Total: 175,825 SF, 1,486 units; facilities in Pleasant Prairie (93,650 SF, 749 units) and West Bend (82,175 SF, 727 units).
Class A institutional-quality assets in southern Wisconsin/Milwaukee MSA; robust investor demand.
stories.summary: Inland Real Estate has acquired two Extra Space-managed self-storage facilities from Bruno's Self Storage in Wisconsin totaling 175,825 SF with 1,486 climate-controlled units. The portfolio includes a 93,650-SF facility completed in 2020 in Pleasant Prairie (749 units) and an 82,175-SF facility completed in 2019 in West Bend (727 units). Both are Class A institutional-quality properties in the rapidly growing southern Wisconsin submarket.
stories.impact: Strong institutional investor demand for Class A self-storage in Milwaukee MSA reflects robust population and household formation in southern Wisconsin; this signals underlying residential demand strength. For multifamily developers, self-storage M&A activity and cap-rate stability in the region validate market fundamentals and suggest multifamily demand remains healthy in Milwaukee and suburban expansion corridors—consider build-to-core apartment sites in Pleasant Prairie and West Bend submarkets.
